study_info.title: Effects of Calcium and Vitamin D Supplementation on Hip Bone Mineral Density and Calcium-Related Analytes in Elderly Ambulatory Australian Women: A Five-Year Randomized Controlled Trial
study_info.authors: Kun Zhu, Amanda Devine, Ian M. Dick, Scott G. Wilson, and Richard L. Prince
study_info.study_design: 5-year randomized, controlled, double-blind trial; randomization was undertaken by a computer-generated randomization sequence with a block size of 12 to the three groups in a ratio of 1:1:1 by an independent research fellow
study_info.inclusion_criteria: aged over 70 yr old, likely to survive a 5-yr study, and not receiving bone active agent
study_info.exclusion_criteria: not likely to survive a 5-yr study, receiving bone active agent
study_info.study_setting: Community-dwelling ambulant women in Perth, Australia

minimal_units.subgroup: all participants; subgroups by baseline 25OHD ≤68 nmol/L and >68 nmol/L; subgroups by baseline PTH ≤3.6 pmol/L and >3.6 pmol/L
minimal_units.intervention_details: 600 mg of calcium as calcium carbonate twice per day with food and 1000 IU of vitamin D2 (ergocalciferol) once per day
minimal_units.intervention_frequency: calcium: twice per day; vitamin D2: once per day
minimal_units.adherence_to_intervention: 86.9% for vitamin D or placebo, 80.7% for calcium or placebo

minimal_units.intervention_details: 600 mg of calcium as calcium carbonate twice per day with food and placebo vitamin D
minimal_units.intervention_frequency: calcium: twice per day; vitamin D placebo: once per day
minimal_units.adherence_to_intervention: 80.9% for calcium or placebo, 84.2% for vitamin D or placebo

minimal_units.control_details: placebo calcium and placebo vitamin D
minimal_units.adherence_to_control: 86.9% for calcium or placebo, 89.8% for vitamin D or placebo
